articleBody:
- [ ] Framing and backing inspection sign-off — Wall studs and blocking must be solid, plumb, and ready to support heavy upper cabinets without flex.
- [ ] Utility rough-in sign-offs for electrical and plumbing — Wire runs, junction boxes, and supply pipes must be inspected and tested before walls are closed up.
- [ ] Moisture-resistant board selection for sink and dishwasher areas — Standard drywall deteriorates when exposed to chronic moisture behind wet zones.
- [ ] Dedicated vapor barrier or insulation placement — Exterior kitchen walls require complete thermal insulation and vapor retarders before hanging sheetrock.
- [ ] Blocking layout map for cabinet installation — Precise measurements showing where solid wood blocking sits ensure cabinet screws hit solid lumber later.
- [ ] Joint compound drying schedule allowances — Rushing mud coats creates cracking, visible tape seams, and weak bonding under new tile backsplashes.
- [ ] Dust containment and appliance protection measures — Drywall sanding dust penetrates cabinetry and appliance components without sealed poly barriers.
- [ ] Smooth finish level confirmation for paint or backsplash — Backsplash areas need flat, sound surfaces, while exposed walls require smooth Level 4 or Level 5 finishes.

How to use this checklist:
Review this list with your contractor before drywall boards are hung. Ensuring hidden plumbing, electrical runs, and framing are inspected before hanging drywall prevents expensive teardowns later.

When extensive plumbing moves or wall alterations are involved, professional installation ensures sturdy, flat walls. Reach out to Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866 to plan your kitchen drywall project.
